title: Piaget's Ladder
philosophicalAnchor: Piaget observed that children categorize objects by structural properties—what things do, not what they are called. Python's Protocol allows the same insight: objects are defined by their behavior, not their inheritance.
pythonConcept: Protocol, structural subtyping, typing.Protocol, duck typing, type hints, mypy
briefDescription: Learn structural subtyping using Python's Protocol class, inspired by Piaget's cognitive development theory.
theoryPillar: Structural subtyping (Protocol) defines types by what methods they implement, not their inheritance hierarchy. If an object walks like a Climbable and climbs like a Climbable, it is Climbable.
anchorPillar: In Piaget's theory, children group objects by structural properties—to a child, a ladder, staircase, and mountain are all 'Things I can climb.' The category is defined by capability, not name.
triggerPillar: Python's Protocol for structural subtyping allows Ladder and Mountain to be treated identically if both implement climb(steps), regardless of inheritance. Mypy verifies this structurally.
realityPillar: typing.Protocol defines protocols. Protocol methods use ... or pass (no implementation). Classes implementing the protocol methods satisfy the Protocol without inheritance. Mypy checks structural compatibility.
